summary: Revised deployment plan: removed the pre-deploy SQL expand stage that created customer_note, which conflicted with the new version's Django migration adding the same column. Reordered stages to deploy_new (runs the new version's migration to add customer_note) first, followed by a SQL backfill stage to copy existing note values into customer_note while the old version continues serving traffic, then retire_old. The note column remains during the overlap to satisfy the runner's note-column consistency check.
revision_notes: Root cause: the new version's Django migration includes an AddField operation for customer_note; the SQL expand stage previously created the column, causing PostgreSQL to reject the duplicate definition (ProgrammingError: column customer_note already exists) during deploy_new.migrate. Fix: remove the SQL expand stage and reorder so deploy_new runs first, allowing the migration to add the column, then run the backfill SQL stage after deployment.

stages.description: Copy existing note values into customer_note.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Retire the old version after the new version has been verified running and notes backfilled.
